sanskrit: tāṃ rātrim uṣitaṃ rāmaṃ sukhotthitam ariṃdamam abravīt prāñjalir vākyaṃ jayaṃ pṛṣṭvā vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: Having passed the night, Rāma — the subduer of foes — rose at ease; Vibhīṣaṇa approached with folded hands, offered felicitations on his victory, and addressed him.

sanskrit: snānāni cāṅgarāgāṇi vastrāṇy ābharaṇāni ca candanāni ca divyāni mālyāni vividhāni ca
english: "Bathing waters, unguents for the body, garments and ornaments, divine sandalwood paste, and garlands of various kinds —

sanskrit: alaṃkāravidaś cemā nāryaḥ padmanibhekṣaṇāḥ upasthitās tvāṃ vidhivat snāpayiṣyanti rāghava
english: — and these women skilled in adornment, with eyes like lotuses, stand ready to bathe you duly according to rite, O Rāghava."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu kākutsthaḥ pratyuvāca vibhīṣaṇam harīn sugrīvamukhyāṃs tvaṃ snānenopanimantraya
english: Thus addressed, Kākutstha replied to Vibhīṣaṇa: "Invite the monkeys headed by Sugrīva to bathe as well."

sanskrit: sa tu tāmyati dharmātmā mamahetoḥ sukhocitaḥ sukumāro mahābāhuḥ kumāraḥ satyasaṃśravaḥ
english: "That righteous-souled one, who deserves comfort, tender-limbed and long-armed, that prince of true vow —

sanskrit: taṃ vinā kaikeyīputraṃ bharataṃ dharmacāriṇam na me snānaṃ bahumataṃ vastrāṇy ābharaṇāni ca
english: — without that son of Kaikeyī, the righteous Bharata, who pines on my account, bathing, garments, and ornaments hold no great value for me.

sanskrit: ita eva pathā kṣipraṃ pratigacchāma tāṃ purīm ayodhyām āyato hy eṣa panthāḥ paramadurgamaḥ
english: Let us proceed swiftly by this very route back to that city, Ayodhyā — for this road, though traversed, is exceedingly difficult."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu kākutsthaṃ pratyuvāca vibhīṣaṇaḥ ahnā tvāṃ prāpayiṣyāmi tāṃ purīṃ pārthivātmaja
english: Thus addressed, Vibhīṣaṇa replied to Kākutstha: "I shall bring you to that city within a single day, O son of a king.

sanskrit: puṣpakaṃ nāma bhadraṃ te vimānaṃ sūryasaṃnibham mama bhrātuḥ kuberasya rāvaṇenāhṛtaṃ balāt
english: The aerial chariot called Puṣpaka — brilliant as the sun — which was forcibly taken from my brother Kubera by Rāvaṇa, bodes well for you.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ meghasaṃkāśaṃ vimānam iha tiṣṭhati tena yāsyasi yānena tvam ayodhyāṃ gajajvaraḥ
english: That chariot, resembling a cloud, stands here; by it, O conqueror of the lordly elephant, you shall travel to Ayodhyā.

sanskrit: ahaṃ te yady anugrāhyo yadi smarasi me guṇān vasa tāvad iha prājña yady asti mayi sauhṛdam
english: If I am worthy of your grace, if you remember my merits, if you have friendship for me — then, O wise one, dwell here for a time.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā vaidehyā cāpi bhāryayā arcitaḥ sarvakāmais tvaṃ tato rāma gamiṣyasi
english: Honoured together with your brother Lakṣmaṇa and your wife Vaidehī with every comfort and desire, then, O Rāma, you shall depart."

sanskrit: prītiyuktas tu me rāma sasainyaḥ sasuhṛdgaṇaḥ satkriyāṃ vihitāṃ tāvad gṛhāṇa tvaṃ mayodyatām
english: "With your army and the assembly of your friends, O Rāma — please accept this hospitality that has been arranged and offered by me with joy.

sanskrit: praṇayād bahumānāc ca sauhṛdena ca rāghava prasādayāmi preṣyo 'haṃ na khalv ājñāpayāmi te
english: Out of affection, deep regard, and friendship, O Rāghava, I am making this plea — I am your servant; I am not issuing you a command."

sanskrit: evam uktas tato rāmaḥ pratyuvāca vibhīṣaṇam rakṣasāṃ vānarāṇāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ copaśṛṇvatām
english: Thus addressed, Rāma then replied to Vibhīṣaṇa within the hearing of all the Rākṣasas and the monkeys:

sanskrit: pūjito 'haṃ tvayā vīra sācivyena paraṃtapa sarvātmanā ca ceṣṭibhiḥ sauhṛdenottamena ca
english: "I have been honoured by you, O hero, O scorcher of foes, through your ministership, through every deed with body and mind, and through your supreme friendship.

sanskrit: na khalv etan na kuryāṃ te vacanaṃ rākṣaseśvara taṃ tu me bhrātaraṃ draṣṭuṃ bharataṃ tvarate manaḥ
english: I would not fail to carry out this word of yours, O lord of Rākṣasas — yet my heart is eager to see my brother Bharata.

sanskrit: māṃ nivartayituṃ yo 'sau citrakūṭam upāgataḥ śirasā yācato yasya vacanaṃ na kṛtaṃ mayā
english: He who came to Citrakūṭa to turn me back, bowing his head in supplication — whose entreaty I did not grant —

sanskrit: kausalyāṃ ca sumitrāṃ ca kaikeyīṃ ca yaśasvinīm gurūṃś ca suhṛdaś caiva paurāṃś ca tanayaiḥ saha
english: — and Kausalyā, Sumitrā, and the illustrious Kaikeyī, my elders and my friends, and the citizens together with their sons —

sanskrit: upasthāpaya me kṣipraṃ vimānaṃ rākṣaseśvara kṛtakāryasya me vāsaḥ kathaṃ cid iha saṃmataḥ
english: — provide for me the chariot swiftly, O lord of Rākṣasas; now that my purpose is fulfilled, residence here is hardly agreeable to me.

sanskrit: anujānīhi māṃ saumya pūjito 'smi vibhīṣaṇa manyur na khalu kartavyas tvaritaś tvānumānaye
english: Grant me leave, O gentle one; I have been honoured, Vibhīṣaṇa — you must not take offence; I take my leave hastily and beg your indulgence.

sanskrit: tataḥ kāñcanacitrāṅgaṃ vaidūryamaṇivedikam kūṭāgāraiḥ parikṣiptaṃ sarvato rajataprabham
english: Then — adorned with golden decorations, furnished with platforms of lapis lazuli, surrounded on all sides by pavilions, radiant with the lustre of silver —

sanskrit: pāṇḍurābhiḥ patākābhiḥ dhvajaiś ca samalaṃkṛtam śobhitaṃ kāñcanair harmyair hemapadmavibhūṣitam
english: — decked with white pennants and standards, beautified with golden mansions, embellished with golden lotuses,

sanskrit: prakīrṇaṃ kiṅkiṇījālair muktāmaṇigavākṣitam ghaṇṭājālaiḥ parikṣiptaṃ sarvato madhurasvanam
english: — strewn with clusters of small bells, with windows inlaid with pearl and gem, encircled by networks of bells giving forth sweet sounds on every side —

sanskrit: tan meruśikharākāraṃ nirmitaṃ viśvakarmaṇā bahubhir bhūṣitaṃ harmyair muktārajatasaṃnibhau
english: — shaped like the peak of Mount Meru, fashioned by Viśvakarman, adorned with many mansions gleaming white with pearl and silver —

sanskrit: talaiḥ sphaṭikacitrāṅgair vaidūryaiś ca varāsanaiḥ mahārhāstaraṇopetair upapannaṃ mahādhanaiḥ
english: — its floors decorated with crystal, with choice seats of lapis lazuli, furnished with rich and costly coverings, endowed with great wealth —

sanskrit: upasthitam anādhṛṣyaṃ tad vimānaṃ manojavam nivedayitvā rāmāya tasthau tatra vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: — that irresistible chariot, swift as thought, was presented to Rāma, and Vibhīṣaṇa stood before him.

sanskrit: upasthitaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā puṣpakaṃ puṣpabhūṣitam avidūre sthitaṃ rāmaṃ pratyuvāca vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: Seeing the Puṣpaka chariot — adorned with flowers — standing near at hand, Vibhīṣaṇa addressed Rāma.

sanskrit: sa tu baddhāñjaliḥ prahvo vinīto rākṣaseśvaraḥ abravīt tvarayopetaḥ kiṃ karomīti rāghavam
english: That lord of Rākṣasas, hands folded, bowing humbly and deferentially, asked Rāghava with urgent solicitude: "What shall I do?"

sanskrit: tam abravīn mahātejā lakṣmaṇasyopaśṛṇvataḥ vimṛśya rāghavo vākyam idaṃ snehapuraskṛtam
english: The great-souled Rāghava, reflecting, spoke these words filled with affection within the hearing of Lakṣmaṇa:

sanskrit: kṛtaprayatnakarmāṇo vibhīṣaṇa vanaukasaḥ ratnair arthaiś ca vivibhair bhūṣaṇaiś cābhipūjaya
english: "The forest-dwelling monkeys who have laboured and exerted themselves — honour them, Vibhīṣaṇa, with jewels, wealth of various kinds, and ornaments.

sanskrit: sahaibhir arditā laṅkā nirjitā rākṣaseśvara hṛṣṭaiḥ prāṇabhayaṃ tyaktvā saṃgrāmeṣv anivartibhiḥ
english: Together with them, O lord of Rākṣasas, Laṅkā has been conquered — by those who, rejoicing, cast aside all fear for their lives and never turned back in battle.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃmānitāś ceme mānārhā mānada tvayā bhaviṣyanti kṛtajñena nirvṛtā hariyūthapāḥ
english: When honoured thus — as they deserve to be honoured — these chiefs of the monkey hosts, O bestower of honour, will become content, gratified by your grateful heart.

sanskrit: tyāginaṃ saṃgrahītāraṃ sānukrośaṃ yaśasvinam yatas tvām avagacchanti tataḥ saṃbodhayāmi te
english: Since they know you as one who is generous, who gathers allies, who is compassionate and illustrious — for that very reason I remind you of this."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa vānarāṃs tān vibhīṣaṇaḥ ratnārthaiḥ saṃvibhāgena sarvān evānvapūjayat
english: Thus addressed by Rāma, Vibhīṣaṇa honoured all those monkeys, distributing jewels and wealth to each.

sanskrit: tatas tān pūjitān dṛṣṭvā ratnair arthaiś ca yūthapān āruroha tato rāmas tad vimānam anuttamam
english: Then, having seen the troop-leaders thus honoured with jewels and wealth, Rāma mounted that supreme chariot.

sanskrit: aṅkenādāya vaidehīṃ lajjamānāṃ yaśasvinīm lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā vikrāntena dhanuṣmatā
english: Taking the illustrious Vaidehī, who was modest with shyness, onto his lap, and accompanied by his heroic, bow-bearing brother Lakṣmaṇa,

sanskrit: abravīc ca vimānasthaḥ kākutsthaḥ sarvavānarān sugrīvaṃ ca mahāvīryaṃ rākṣasaṃ ca vibhīṣaṇam
english: Kākutstha, seated in the chariot, addressed all the monkeys and the mighty Sugrīva and the Rākṣasa Vibhīṣaṇa:

sanskrit: mitrakāryaṃ kṛtam idaṃ bhavadbhir vānarottamāḥ anujñātā mayā sarve yatheṣṭaṃ pratigacchata
english: "The duty of friends has been performed by you, O foremost of monkeys; you are all dismissed by me — depart, each as you wish."

sanskrit: yat tu kāryaṃ vayasyena suhṛdā vā paraṃtapa kṛtaṃ sugrīva tat sarvaṃ bhavatā dharmabhīruṇā kiṣkindhāṃ pratiyāhy āśu svasainyenābhisaṃvṛtaḥ
english: "O scorcher of foes, Sugrīva — all that befits a comrade and a friend has been done by you, who are ever reverent of dharma; return swiftly to Kiṣkindhā, surrounded by your own army.

sanskrit: svarājye vasa laṅkāyāṃ mayā datte vibhīṣaṇa na tvāṃ dharṣayituṃ śaktāḥ sendrā api divaukasaḥ
english: Dwell in sovereignty over Laṅkā, given by me to you, Vibhīṣaṇa — not even the gods together with Indra are capable of assailing you.

sanskrit: ayodhyāṃ pratiyāsyāmi rājadhānīṃ pitur mama abhyanujñātum icchāmi sarvān āmantrayāmi vaḥ
english: I am about to return to Ayodhyā, my father's royal capital; I wish to take your leave — I bid farewell to you all."

sanskrit: evam uktās tu rāmeṇa vānarās te mahābalāḥ ūcuḥ prāñjalayo rāmaṃ rākṣasaś ca vibhīṣaṇaḥ ayodhyāṃ gantum icchāmaḥ sarvān nayatu no bhavān
english: Thus addressed by Rāma, those immensely powerful monkeys and the Rākṣasa Vibhīṣaṇa replied with folded hands: "We wish to go to Ayodhyā — let your honour lead all of us."

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tvām abhiṣekārdraṃ kausalyām abhivādya ca acireṇāgamiṣyāmaḥ svān gṛhān nṛpateḥ suta
english: "Having seen you consecrated with the coronation waters, and having paid homage to Kausalyā, we shall before long return to our own homes, O son of the king."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu dharmātmā vānaraiḥ savibhīṣaṇaiḥ abravīd rāghavaḥ śrīmān sasugrīvavibhīṣaṇān
english: Thus addressed by the monkeys together with Vibhīṣaṇa, the righteous-souled, illustrious Rāghava spoke to them — Sugrīva and Vibhīṣaṇa among them:

sanskrit: priyāt priyataraṃ labdhaṃ yad ahaṃ sasuhṛjjanaḥ sarvair bhavadbhiḥ sahitaḥ prītiṃ lapsye purīṃ gataḥ
english: "What is dearer than the dear has been gained by me — accompanied by my friends and together with all of you, I shall experience joy upon reaching my city.

sanskrit: kṣipram āroha sugrīva vimānaṃ vānaraiḥ saha tvam adhyāroha sāmātyo rākṣasendravibhīṣaṇa
english: Board the chariot swiftly, Sugrīva, together with your monkeys; you too ascend, Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of Rākṣasas, along with your ministers."

sanskrit: tatas tat puṣpakaṃ divyaṃ sugrīvaḥ saha senayā adhyārohat tvarañ śīghraṃ sāmātyaś ca vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: Then Sugrīva together with his army swiftly and quickly ascended that divine Puṣpaka chariot, as did Vibhīṣaṇa with his ministers.

sanskrit: teṣv ārūḍheṣu sarveṣu kauberaṃ paramāsanam rāghaveṇābhyanujñātam utpapāta vihāyasaṃ
english: When all of them had boarded, that supreme vehicle of Kubera, permitted to rise by Rāghava, soared aloft into the sky.

sanskrit: yayau tena vimānena haṃsayuktena bhāsvatā prahṛṣṭaś ca pratītaś ca babhau rāmaḥ kuberavat
english: Rāma, filled with delight and elation, travelled in that resplendent chariot yoked with swans, and shone like Kubera himself.

sanskrit: anujñātaṃ tu rāmeṇa tad vimānam anuttamam utpapāta mahāmeghaḥ śvasanenoddhato yathā
english: That supreme chariot, set in motion by Rāma, soared upward like a great cloud lifted by the wind.

sanskrit: pātayitvā tataś cakṣuḥ sarvato raghunandanaḥ abravīn maithilīṃ sītāṃ rāmaḥ śaśinibhānanām
english: Then the joy of the Raghu line, Rāma, cast his gaze in every direction and addressed Maithilī Sītā, whose face resembled the moon:

sanskrit: kailāsaśikharākāre trikūṭaśikhare sthitām laṅkām īkṣasva vaidehi nirmitāṃ viśvakarmaṇā
english: "Look, O Vaidehī, upon Laṅkā, standing upon the peak of Trikūṭa whose shape resembles the summit of Kailāsa — built by Viśvakarman.

sanskrit: etad āyodhanaṃ paśya māṃsaśoṇitakardamam harīṇāṃ rākṣasānāṃ ca sīte viśasanaṃ mahat
english: Behold this battlefield, O Sītā — turned to a mire of flesh and blood — the great slaughter-ground of the monkeys and Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: tavahetor viśālākṣi rāvaṇo nihato mayā kumbhakarṇo 'tra nihataḥ prahastaś ca niśācaraḥ
english: For your sake, O large-eyed one, Rāvaṇa was slain by me; Kumbhakarṇa was slain here, and the night-roaming Prahasta as well.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇenendrajic cātra rāvaṇir nihato raṇe virūpākṣaś ca duṣprekṣyo mahāpārśvamahodarau
english: Indrajit, son of Rāvaṇa — also called Rāvaṇi — was slain in battle here by Lakṣmaṇa, and also the dreadful-eyed Virūpākṣa, Mahāpārśva, and Mahōdara.

sanskrit: akampanaś ca nihato balino 'nye ca rākṣasāḥ triśirāś cātikāyaś ca devāntakanarāntakau
english: Akampana too was slain here, and other powerful Rākṣasas — Triśiras, Atikāya, Devāntaka, and Narāntaka.

sanskrit: atra mandodarī nāma bhāryā taṃ paryadevayat sapatnīnāṃ sahasreṇa sāsreṇa parivāritā
english: Here Mandodarī, his wife by name, lamented for him, surrounded by a thousand fellow-wives, all weeping.

sanskrit: etat tu dṛśyate tīrthaṃ samudrasya varānane yatra sāgaram uttīrya tāṃ rātrim uṣitā vayam
english: That ford of the ocean is visible here, O fairest one, where, having crossed the sea, we spent the night.

sanskrit: eṣa setur mayā baddhaḥ sāgare salilārṇave tavahetor viśālākṣi nalasetuḥ suduṣkaraḥ
english: This bridge was built by me across the ocean, the water-flood — for your sake, O large-eyed one — the bridge of Nala, most difficult to construct.

sanskrit: paśya sāgaram akṣobhyaṃ vaidehi varuṇālayam apāram abhigarjantaṃ śaṅkhaśuktiniṣevitam
english: Behold the imperturbable ocean, O Vaidehī — the abode of Varuṇa — roaring boundlessly, frequented by conches and oysters.

sanskrit: hiraṇyanābhaṃ śailendraṃ kāñcanaṃ paśya maithili viśramārthaṃ hanumato bhittvā sāgaram utthitam
english: Look, O Maithilī, at that golden mountain, king of mountains, with a golden navel — which rose out of the ocean after splitting it, to give Hanūmat a place to rest.

sanskrit: atra rākṣasarājo 'yam ājagāma vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: Here came this king of Rākṣasas, Vibhīṣaṇa, to offer himself.

sanskrit: eṣā sā dṛśyate sīte kiṣkindhā citrakānanā sugrīvasya purī ramyā yatra vālī mayā hataḥ
english: That city visible yonder, O Sītā, is Kiṣkindhā, with its colourful woodlands — Sugrīva's charming city, where Vālī was slain by me.

sanskrit: dṛśyate 'sau mahān sīte savidyud iva toyadaḥ ṛśyamūko giriśreṣṭhaḥ kāñcanair dhātubhir vṛtaḥ
english: That great mountain gleaming like a cloud with lightning is visible yonder, O Sītā — Ṛśyamūka, finest of mountains, clad in golden minerals.

sanskrit: atrāhaṃ vānarendreṇa sugrīveṇa samāgataḥ samayaś ca kṛtaḥ sīte vadhārthaṃ vālino mayā
english: Here I met Sugrīva, lord of monkeys, and here, O Sītā, the compact was made by me for the slaying of Vālī.

sanskrit: eṣā sā dṛśyate pampā nalinī citrakānanā tvayā vihīno yatrāhaṃ vilalāpa suduḥkhitaḥ
english: That is the Pampā lake visible yonder, adorned with lotuses and colourful woodlands — where I, bereft of you, lamented in deep anguish.

sanskrit: asyās tīre mayā dṛṣṭā śabarī dharmacāriṇī atra yojanabāhuś ca kabandho nihato mayā
english: On the bank of this lake I encountered the righteous Śabarī; and here Kabandha — with arms extending a yojana — was slain by me.

sanskrit: dṛśyate 'sau janasthāne sīte śrīmān vanaspatiḥ yatra yuddhaṃ mahad vṛttaṃ tavahetor vilāsini rāvaṇasya nṛśaṃsasya jaṭāyoś ca mahātmanaḥ
english: That splendid forest tree in Janasthāna is visible yonder, O Sītā, O graceful one — the place where the great battle occurred for your sake between the cruel Rāvaṇa and the great-souled Jaṭāyus.

sanskrit: kharaś ca nihataś saṃkhye dūṣaṇaś ca nipātitaḥ triśirāś ca mahāvīryo mayā bāṇair ajihmagaiḥ
english: There Khara was slain in combat, Dūṣaṇa was laid low, and the mighty Triśiras was felled by me with unerring arrows.

sanskrit: parṇaśālā tathā citrā dṛśyate śubhadarśanā yatra tvaṃ rākṣasendreṇa rāvaṇena hṛtā balāt
english: That lovely, beautiful leaf-hut is also visible there — the place from which you were violently abducted by Rāvaṇa, lord of Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: eṣā godāvarī ramyā prasannasalilā śivā agastyasyāśramo hy eṣa dṛśyate paśya maithili
english: This is the lovely Godāvarī, with clear, auspicious waters; and this visible here is the hermitage of Agastya — behold it, O Maithilī.

sanskrit: vaidehi dṛśyate cātra śarabhaṅgāśramo mahān upayātaḥ sahasrākṣo yatra śakraḥ puraṃdaraḥ
english: The great hermitage of Śarabhaṅga is also visible here, O Vaidehī — the place to which the thousand-eyed Śakra, the smasher of citadels, himself came.

sanskrit: ete te tāpasāvāsā dṛśyante tanumadhyame atriḥ kulapatir yatra sūryavaiśvānaraprabhaḥ atra sīte tvayā dṛṣṭā tāpasī dharmacāriṇī
english: These dwelling-places of ascetics are visible yonder, O slender-waisted one — where Atri the patriarch of his lineage shines with the splendour of sun and fire; and here, O Sītā, you encountered the righteous ascetic woman.

sanskrit: asmin deśe mahākāyo virādho nihato mayā
english: In this very place the great-bodied Virādha was slain by me.

sanskrit: asau sutanuśailendraś citrakūṭaḥ prakāśate yatra māṃ kaikayīputraḥ prasādayitum āgataḥ
english: That slender and majestic peak gleaming yonder is Citrakūṭa — the place where the son of Kaikeyī came to placate me.

sanskrit: eṣā sā yamunā dūrād dṛśyate citrakānanā bharadvājāśramo yatra śrīmān eṣa prakāśate
english: That is the Yamunā visible in the distance, with its picturesque woodlands; and here the splendid hermitage of Bharadvāja gleams before us.

sanskrit: eṣā tripathagā gaṅgā dṛśyate varavarṇini śṛṅgaverapuraṃ caitad guho yatra samāgataḥ
english: This is the Gaṅgā flowing in three streams, visible to you, O fairest of complexion; and this is Śṛṅgaverapura, the place where we met Guha.

sanskrit: eṣā sā dṛśyate 'yodhyā rājadhānī pitur mama ayodhyāṃ kuru vaidehi praṇāmaṃ punar āgatā
english: That visible yonder is Ayodhyā, my father's royal capital — make your obeisance to Ayodhyā, O Vaidehī, for you have returned.

sanskrit: tatas te vānarāḥ sarve rākṣasaś ca vibhīṣaṇaḥ utpatyotpatya dadṛśus tāṃ purīṃ śubhadarśanām
english: Then all those monkeys and the Rākṣasa Vibhīṣaṇa, leaping up again and again, beheld that beautiful city.

sanskrit: tatas tu tāṃ pāṇḍuraharmyamālinīṃ viśālakakṣyāṃ gajavājisaṃkulām purīm ayodhyāṃ dadṛśuḥ plavaṃgamāḥ purīṃ mahendrasya yathāmarāvatīm
english: Then those monkeys beheld the city of Ayodhyā — encircled by white mansions, with its broad enclosures thronged with elephants and horses — even as the gods behold the city of Mahendra, Amarāvatī.
